title: fix(app-shell): an Interfaces leaf save clears the refusal strip an earlier save showed (objectui#11950)
body:
Fixes #11950

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`InterfacesPillar`'s leaf `doSave` (in `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx`) now calls `setError(null)` at the start of each save: right after `setSaving('draft')` and before the request, where the Data and Automations pillars' `doSave` reset theirs. A refused save still sets its own refusal in the `catch`. No other region of the file changed.

Before this change, the `catch` set the pillar's `error` and only a leaf (re)load cleared it. After a refused leaf save, the red "Changes not saved" strip stayed once a later save went through, until the author left the leaf.

Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MgfduSkFrfM3eorB3UGfAU` (os-dev, seat `domain:ui#2`, claim comment 6060793465).

## How the PM's mechanism hypotheses held up

- **H1 confirmed.** `DataPillar`'s and `AutomationsPillar`'s `doSave` both call `setError(null)` right after `setSaving('draft')`, before the `try` that sends the request. They reset before the request, not on success only. This change adds the reset at that same place. Pin 3 holds the placement: the strip is gone while the save is still in flight.
- **H2: the held hint is separate state.** The held notice is `leafHeld`, computed by `dashboardHeldEdit` over the buffer (objectui#11910) and rendered by `StudioHeldNotice`. The refusal is `error`, rendered by `StudioRefusalStrip`. The reset cannot reach the held line, and `metadataError.ts` is not involved. The pillar does not allow "a successful save of another leaf" beside a held one, because it holds only the open leaf's buffer (objectui#11272). The nearest sequence it does allow is an unbound widget added on the same leaf while a save is in flight. Pin 3 covers it.
- **H3.** Pins 1 and 2 are the two pins triage asked for.

## Pins

The new file is `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/InterfacesPillar.saveErrorClears-11950.test.tsx`. It is mounted like the objectui#11910 held-widget pins: the real `DashboardPreview` and `DashboardWidgetInspector`, and a client double that scripts each dashboard save (refuse, hold in flight, or accept).

1. A refused save, then a save that goes through, leaves no strip.
2. CONTROL: a second refused save still shows its own refusal. The strip's Details show the second issue and not the first, and there is one strip.
3. A save in flight clears the refusal as it is sent. It does not clear the hold raised by an edit taken meanwhile: the held line and the inspector hint stay, and nothing more is sent.

**Ablation.** The fix was committed first. The mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, and the restore was proven by the blob hash matching HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. With the reset removed, pin 1 (`the saved draft shows no refusal`) and pin 3 (`cleared as the save is sent, ...`) go red, and pin 2 stays green. That is the expected direction: `Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)`. A first attempt ran nothing: the tool refused it before writing, because its replacement was a substring of its anchor. The second attempt used a marker comment, and the mutation landed (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed).

## Gates

Run at `a9be0f721` (HEAD, after the last commit). The ablation ran at `cc3beebe8`, whose source files are byte-identical to HEAD's; the commit after it adds only the changeset.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` from the repo root, over every `StudioDesignSurface*` and `InterfacesPillar*` test file listed by `git ls-tree HEAD` (69 files: the new one, the objectui#11910 `heldWidget` pins and `heldWidgetPublish`), plus `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/column-identity.ratchet.test.ts`: `Test Files  70 passed (70)`, `Tests  405 passed (405)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`, after `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...'` (`Tasks: 28 successful, 28 total`): exit 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new test file.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0, `2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/11950-interfaces-save-error.md.`
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: exit 0, `No changeset declares a major bump.`
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only`, exit 0.
- `pnpm check:control-bytes`: exit 0, OK.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the two touched `.tsx` files: exit 0, 0 errors. The new test has 0 warnings. `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` has 13 warnings, the same count and rules as its base blob linted through `--stdin`.
- Also run, because the new test mocks modules and the change adds a changeset: `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`. All exit 0.
- Eager-closure budget: NOT MEASURED locally, because it needs a console build. The budget bot's reading on this PR is the one that counts.

Patch changeset for `@object-ui/app-shell`. Nothing is added to the package entry. No docs change: no guide or README describes how long the Interfaces refusal strip stays.

## Acceptance notes

- **The app re-read failure shares the pillar's `error`, and the canvas tells the two apart through it.** This was measured with an uncommitted probe on the real `InterfacesPillar`, with a host that bumps `draftNonce` on `onDraftSaved` as the surface does, and a client double whose second `list('app')` throws. It was not measured against a live server. Here is the sequence. A draft save lands, and the app re-read that follows fails. The app-load effect's `catch` sets `error` and `appStatus: 'missing'`, and the strip says "Service unavailable".
  - Before this change: that strip stays after the next save lands and the next re-read succeeds. It is the same stale-strip family as this card. The app-load effect never clears `error` on success.
  - After this change: the next leaf save clears it as it is sent. While that save is in flight, `appStatus === 'missing' && !error` holds, so the canvas shows "This package has no app yet" in place of the open leaf. The canvas comes back, with no strip, once the save lands and the re-read succeeds.
  - Where it would land: the app-load effect, which treats a failed re-read of the same app as "no app" and never clears its error on success. That region is outside this claim's file surface, so it is reported to the seat and not changed here.
